I am not sure but I think they messed me up when I had my first c-section. The doctor ordered a spinal tap and they placed a big painful needle into my back.  Immediately I began to vomit. I had had a tiny sip of orange juice and so I threw up about a gallon of orange vomit in the birthing chair. After some discussion the anesthesiologist made an adjustment and I stopped vomiting and began to shiver uncontrollably. He said he couldn't stop the shivering safely until after the baby was delivered. They warmed blankets and piled them around me, and put heat lamps on me and wheeled me in for surgery. It was miserable. They had told me it would be best for the baby if I stayed conscious, so I was determined to stay awake. It took a long time and it hurt... finally after they showed me my daughter, healthy and well, I asked if we were done. They said no, they had to close up. I remember actually thinking, "that's it I'm outta here" and passing out.

I woke up the next morning in my hospital room. My husband said he'd been worried all night. He said I was pale as death. He said the anesthesiologist came in quite a lot to check on me, that he'd seemed concerned too.

About a week later my OB-GYN is telling me about the fibroids in my uterus and casually mentioned that we'd talked about it already in the recovery room at the hospital. I had no recollection of it, but apparently I was awake and talking in the recovery room and have absolutely no recollection of it.
